resources.string: Device capabilities, on-device decoder benchmark, recorded sessions and A/B comparison
Decoder, low latency mode, buffering, processing priority and statistics. Resolution, FPS, bitrate and presentation sync (frame pacing) are in Basic Settings.
%s\nResyncs (IDR) only when the decoder can\'t keep up and frames pile up. Network-only delay is never acted upon.
%s\nPriority of the video receive, submit and render threads.

Direct SurfaceView output: the decoder writes into the display surface (hardware overlay, no copies, no color conversion). OpenGL ES, Vulkan and TextureView would add a GPU pass and at least one frame of latency, so they are not offered.
Per-stage latency breakdown (mean / p95) when the performance overlay is enabled
Save a per-stage latency report after every stream so configurations can be compared
Also save the timings of every frame (up to 10 minutes per session)

Saves the decoded frame as a PNG in the report folder (ull-sessions/<version>/) to compare it with screenshots of the PC. It does not include the box\'s own video processing. Leave it off when measuring latency.
The video capture is black: this device does not let apps read the video (%1$s)
Re-applies the Ultra Low Latency profile and resets the advanced latency settings
Restore the default latency settings? Gamepad, input and UI settings are not changed.
All vendor keys: some decoders may reject this configuration. Moonlight then falls back automatically; run the decoder benchmark to verify it actually helps on this device.
Network: frame receive %1$s · jitter %2$.2f ms · queue delay %3$s · %4$.1f Mbps
Frame size: %1$.0f / %2$.0f kB (p50/p95) · cap ≈ %3$.0f kB · at cap %4$s
WARNING: the decoder can\'t sustain this stream. Lower FPS, resolution or bitrate.
Display without ALLM (TV: enable Game mode; PC monitor: nothing to do)

The display (%1$s) does not advertise ALLM (automatic game mode). If it is a TV, enable its Game mode manually: TV picture processing can add tens of milliseconds. PC monitors usually don\'t process the image and need nothing.
%1$d Mbps on %2$d Mbps Ethernet: a full-size frame (~%3$.0f kB) takes ~%4$.1f ms to arrive (20 Mbps: ~%5$.1f ms). Try HEVC first.
WARNING: sustained network queueing. Lower the bitrate or check the network.

Reports are saved in:
%1$s

1. Run the device capability report (send it if the device needs analysis).
2. Run the H.264 decoder benchmark: it measures every MediaCodec low latency configuration on this device and the "Auto" mode will use the fastest one that works.
3. Stream with different profiles and compare the recorded sessions.
No sessions recorded yet. Enable \"Record session reports\" and stream for at least a few seconds.
At least two recorded sessions are needed.
Decoder benchmark results cleared. \"Auto\" will use Moonlight\'s heuristics until the benchmark is run again.
Decoder benchmark %1$s — watch the frame counter: within each run it must move smoothly
Did the frame counter move smoothly within every run? (Restarting at 0 when a run begins and a short stop when it ends are normal.)
Confirmed. "Auto" will use the measured configuration (for Amlogic HEVC this replaces the safety rule).
Result discarded. "Auto" keeps Moonlight\'s heuristics and the safety rules.
B-A is the difference. \"+\" means B is better, \"-\" means B is worse. n/a: not measured in one of the sessions.
